_note: The backend-swap acceptance policy for ONE named profile, as data the gate executes rather than prose a reader is trusted to apply. This file was rewritten on 2026-08-04 because its predecessor was bound only by `recorded_refine_rounds: 3` -- refine rounds alone do not name a backend, an output profile, an oracle or a DPI, and the four D2 findings it carried had been measured at a different profile altogether. `backend_parity.py` refused to adjudicate against it and said so. The refusal was right: floors measured at one full profile say nothing about another, and `--update-policy` deliberately will not migrate findings across that boundary. So this is a NEW policy bound to `pdfium/gdocs/none/refine0@240dpi`, populated from a fresh measurement run, and it is PROVISIONAL: it authorises nothing. The findings were measured at ff518be. c1cbc2a has since retired c2_paper2col (see `provisional_shortfalls._retired`) and no canonical parity run has been recorded against that tree, so this file is one run behind HEAD. The floors that remain still describe it -- that commit reports the other 15 documents unchanged on every dimension -- but re-record with `--update-policy` at the next canonical opportunity rather than trusting that indefinitely.

dy_absolute_exemption._note: A dy_p50 delta is not a regression when BOTH arms are already under the ceiling, PROVIDED within2pt did not move adversely on the same document. Why the magnitude rule is needed: dy_p50's margin is proportional (10% of the reference) with a 0.5pt floor, so near zero the floor is the entire rule and a document can go 0.04pt -> 1.29pt and be graded a regression over a fraction of one line's leading. Below about two points the number is reporting the ascent convention of whoever measured the glyph tops rather than any placement a reader could see -- see `_ascent_artifact` below and docs/dy-ascent-artifact.md. Why the CONDITION is not optional: within2pt counts the words actually landing within 2pt of source, so it states directly what dy_p50 only proxies, and dy and within2pt demonstrably move in opposite directions -- x02_lo_report_toc moves dy 8.3 -> 13.1 while within2pt IMPROVES 0.0608 -> 0.1877. An unconditioned magnitude rule would excuse a document whose placement genuinely degraded, which is the whole failure mode this policy exists to prevent. Keyed by FULL profile ID and never borrowed: dy at the shipping settings and at the candidate profile are different distributions through different renderers, and the refusal to adjudicate across profile boundaries stays. `adjudicate` selects only the entry matching the run's profile, so a section for a profile this policy does not govern is recorded but inert.
dy_absolute_exemption._not_widened: The ceiling is 2.0pt and must not be raised. Absorbing the next divergences up would need roughly 13pt (x02_lo_report_toc), 21pt (x07_chrome_memo_running), 17pt (x10_chrome_tables_plain) and 68pt (y17_rfc9110). Floors that large would blind the policy to four genuine structural divergences, which are tracked as the pdfium line-segmentation convergence campaign. 2.0pt was not chosen to make anything pass: at the shipping settings the exempted values top out at 1.49pt and the next dy magnitude in the corpus is c3_tables at 2.75pt, already graded `same`, so the ceiling sits in empty space rather than just above a failure.

pdfium/gdocs/none/refine0@240dpi.reason: At the candidate profile the rule clears exactly one document: x13_rl_report_running, dy 0.85 -> 1.36 with within2pt 0.4825 -> 0.4389 (inside its 0.08 margin) and no other dimension worse. It is the only base-14 document in its class here. Every other dy regression at this profile is an order of magnitude larger and structural.

pymupdf/standard/libreoffice/refine3@240.reason: At the shipping settings FIVE gated base-14 documents carry a dy_p50 regression inside the 2.0pt ceiling -- 01 (0.5 -> 1.38), 02 (0.04 -> 1.29), 03 (0.54 -> 1.49), 05 (0.59 -> 1.39) and f1 (0.0 -> 1.2) -- but the rule clears only THREE of them. 02_research_paper and 03_tech_report_code are held back by the condition: their within2pt collapses 0.7614 -> 0.5685 and 0.4602 -> 0.2803, far outside the 0.08 margin, so their placement really did degrade and the magnitude rule must not excuse it. Both keep a MAJOR verdict on within2pt with or without this exemption, so the condition costs nothing in outcome and states the truth instead of a convenient count. This entry is recorded for the product-bound policy that does not yet exist; this file is bound to the candidate profile, so `adjudicate` never selects it here.

_ascent_artifact: Why small dy differences are a measurement convention rather than a placement error (task #22, decision recorded). dy is computed on GLYPH TOPS. PyMuPDF reads the declared base-14 ascent -- Helvetica is 1.070-1.075em -- while PDFium substitutes a generic ~0.905em, so the same baseline yields an apparent vertical offset of about 0.17 x type size: 1.8pt at 10.5pt text. The BASELINES are identical; only the reported tops differ. DECISION: the metric definition stays glyph-tops. Redefining it to baselines would be a simultaneous baseline event across the gate, this parity policy and every live-pass record, invalidating three independent bodies of committed evidence at once to fix a reporting convention. The artifact is instead absorbed by the 2.0pt exemption above and documented in docs/dy-ascent-artifact.md. This resolves the decision item in task #22.

This section is for documents where the two backends disagree about what CORRECT means and the candidate was verified to be the right one -- and nothing enters it without rendered evidence, because a document listed here is excused from the comparison. `c4_i18n` and `c5_graphics` were waived here under the previous, differently-bound policy, and both of those waivers rest on rendered evidence that was produced at the parity/refine3 profile. That evidence has NOT been reproduced at `pdfium/gdocs/none/refine0@240dpi`. Re-verify with rendered output at this profile before promoting either one back.

margins._note: How much worse the candidate may be on a dimension before the document counts as a regression. Every gated dimension appears here, and each is judged INDEPENDENTLY -- the comparison used to stop at the first dimension outside its margin, so one improvement suppressed every regression ordered after it. Sizing: these are deliberately looser than testkit/gate.py's run-to-run tolerances, because two correct parsers legitimately differ by more than one parser differs from itself; the ratio is about 2.5-5x on the fraction metrics. They are NOT tuned to make the current corpus pass -- a margin chosen to clear a failure is the failure, silenced. dy_p50 additionally carries gate.py's 10% relative term, since it is the one dimension that is not a fraction and runs from 0.3pt to 34pt across this corpus. UNCHANGED on 2026-08-04: rebinding a policy to a profile is not an occasion to move a margin, and moving one in the same change would make the rebinding unreviewable.

provisional_shortfalls._note: Documents where the candidate is measurably worse at this profile AFTER the margins above are applied, the cause is attributed, and the shortfall is PROVISIONAL: visible and bounded, but it may NOT authorise a backend swap or a release (plan section 17 rule 4). Acceptance is bounded in both directions by the numeric floors: worsening past one fails, and clearing the divergence entirely fails as a stale record. Ratifying one means moving it to `ratified_shortfalls` with ratified_by, ratified_on, issue and review_condition -- all four required, all four checked. The decision is scheduled for the Google Docs checkpoint (DEC-D2), because Google Docs is the renderer this project actually targets and LibreOffice is a proxy for it.
provisional_shortfalls._retired: c2_paper2col.pdf was tracked here when this policy was written and was RETIRED the same day by ebcb3be (merged as c1cbc2a), which absorbs a superscript into its host line in the PDFium parser rather than leaving it a line -- and a block -- of its own. That commit records the candidate moving dy_p50 23.55 -> 10.00 against a 10.05 reference, within2pt 0.0131 -> 0.1247 against 0.1039, and live_text_cov, word_recall and raster_frac all reaching the reference exactly. No dimension is worse any more, so the document is now BETTER and the entry described nothing. Keeping it would have been a stale waiver, which `adjudicate()` fails on by design: a waiver for a difference that no longer exists still excuses the document, and would hide the next real regression on it. Deleted rather than re-floored -- floors are recorded by `--update-policy` on the canonical environment, and no such run has happened against the new tree. The c4/c5 floors below are untouched and still describe it: that commit reports the other 15 documents unchanged on every dimension.

ratified_shortfalls._note: A shortfall reaches this section only when a named owner takes responsibility for it on a date, with an issue and a review or expiry condition -- `ratified_by`, `ratified_on`, `issue`, `review_condition`, all four required and all four checked by `adjudicate`. Ratified does NOT mean fixed. Both entries below are still real divergences, still bounded by floors in both directions, and clearing one entirely still fails as a stale record, because a waiver for a difference that no longer exists would excuse the document and hide the next regression on it. c4_i18n.pdf.review_condition: Retire when PDFium stops falling back to raster on the complex-script region: raster_frac returning to 0.0 with live_text_cov back at 1.0 makes this entry describe nothing, `adjudicate` reports it stale, and every run blocks until it is deleted -- so retirement is enforced rather than remembered. Re-open the decision, do not widen the floors, if raster_frac rises above 0.0909 or live_text_cov falls below 0.9091. This ratifies ONE measured fallback on ONE document, not complex-script handling in general, and a different cause on this document is a different decision.
c4_i18n.pdf.measured_commit_source: the commit stamped into docs/evidence/canonical-gate-2026-08-04.json by the canonical run that produced these numbers
c4_i18n.pdf.reason: Complex-script raster fallback. One region in eleven falls back to raster under PDFium (raster_frac 0 -> 0.0909), and the text in it stops counting as live (1.0 -> 0.9091). Content recall barely moves (0.9832 -> 0.9748), which is the signature of a rasterised region rather than lost text. PRIOR EVIDENCE, at the parity/refine3 profile and not reproduced here: PDFium reports RTL glyphs in logical order, which is what a DOCX must carry, while PyMuPDF returns visual order, so the incumbent's DOCX renders Arabic backwards -- verified by rendering the source and both outputs side by side. On that evidence the candidate is the correct backend for this document and the live-text loss is the price of a raster fallback rather than a defect in ordering. Until that rendering is reproduced at THIS profile, the difference is tracked and blocking, not excused.

c5_graphics.pdf.review_condition: Retire when the designed-page limitation is lifted and PDFium no longer rasterises more of this page than PyMuPDF: raster_frac returning to 0.2933 or below makes this entry stale and blocks until deleted. Re-open the decision, do not widen the floors, if raster_frac exceeds 0.3222 or doc_recall falls below 0.6556. Note the metric caveat recorded in `reason` -- live_text_cov scores the INCUMBENT higher here because invisible white text still counts as live, so this ratification accepts a measured number that understates the candidate's actual output. c5_graphics remains a deliberately deferred designed-page limitation; ratifying the divergence does not un-defer it, it records that the deferral is accepted while it stands.
c5_graphics.pdf.measured_commit_source: the commit stamped into docs/evidence/canonical-gate-2026-08-04.json by the canonical run that produced these numbers
c5_graphics.pdf.reason: Designed-page rasterisation. PDFium rasterises one region more than PyMuPDF on a gradient/rounded/rotated designed page (0.2933 -> 0.3222). METRIC CAVEAT, and it points the other way: live_text_cov scores the incumbent higher (0.7067 against 0.6778) because invisible white text still counts as live. Text coverage cannot see contrast. PRIOR EVIDENCE, at the parity/refine3 profile and not reproduced here: the page opens with a gradient band carrying white text; PyMuPDF does not report the gradient, so the band's text is emitted white on white and is invisible, while PDFium reports the pattern flattened to grey and the heading survives legibly. Both arms are page_err 1 here, so the floor permits it: c5_graphics is the deliberately deferred designed-page limitation, and the floor bounds it rather than pretending it is fixed.
